html:
The Cushites are the peoples who speak Cushitic languages, a branch of the Afroasiatic family, across the Horn of Africa. The map uses the name in its 900 snapshot for the dry lowlands of what are now Somalia and eastern Ethiopia, the same area it labels Kushites in 700.

The largest Cushitic peoples today are the Oromo, the Somali, the Afar and, in Sudan, the Beja. Around 900 the eastern lowlands were home to herding clans who moved with their camels and flocks between wells and pastures.

On the coast, ports such as Zeila traded across the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean, and Islam spread from them inland. The highlands to the west were held by the Christian heirs of Aksum. The later Muslim sultanates of the region, such as Ifat and Adal, grew out of this world.
